Every AI model suddenly looks replaceable, and picking the right one has turned into a second job. This video is a practical model picker: how to choose which AI to use for real work without overpaying or drowning in model names.

My Links 🔗
👉🏻 Newsletter: https://natesnewsletter.substack.com/
👉🏻 X: https://x.com/natebjones
👉🏻 TikTok:   / nate.b.jones  
👉🏻 Instagram:   / nate.b.jones  

What's really happening when every AI model suddenly looks replaceable?

The common story is that the smartest model wins. The real question is which intelligence a specific job actually needs.

In this video, I share the inside scoop on how to pick the right AI for the work in front of you:

Why daily-driver models differ from cheap workhorse models like GLM 5.2
How to route familiar work to cheaper models and review it fast
What to keep on a frontier model when the shape of the job is unclear
Where specialists win: images, video, live web, and coding harnesses

The models will keep changing, but if you route by the job and keep your context portable, no single model going away can stall your work.

text:
GET THE SKILL: https://brad-b.kit.com/5ca85f4a2a
WORK WITH ME: https://cal.com/bradley-bonanno/ai-st...

Claude Code can't watch videos - until you give it the /watch skill. Paste a link and Claude pulls the frames and the transcript together, so it understands what happens on screen and when. It demolished a 2-hour interview in seconds, and it works on YouTube, Zoom recordings, Looms, TikToks, local files — over 1,600 sites. The skill is free on GitHub, and v2 is the biggest upgrade since launch: 40x faster, cheaper, and it handles ultra-long videos.

In this video I walk through everything new in v2. Smart scene selection picks the frames that actually matter instead of sampling blindly. Deictic targeting means when a speaker says "look at this," Claude finds the exact frame they're pointing at. Token burner mode takes the cap off entirely for maximum detail when you need it. The new efficient keyframe mode pulls keyframes straight out of the video file instead of rebuilding every frame — that's where the 40x comes from. And frame deduplication strips near-identical frames (a talking head barely changes) so you stop paying tokens for the same picture twice — half the comments on v1 were about token costs, so this one's for you. Then I show the full install and upgrade: two commands, two minutes, plus the first-run mode picker so you know exactly which of the four modes to choose.

0:00 — Claude just watched a 2-hour video in seconds
2:14 — Smart scene selection

3:53 — Efficient mode
5:15 — Frame deduplication (cheaper tokens)
